newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt faces large protest on national day.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt faces large protest on national day.

text.p: Tens of thousands of protestors chanted anti-government slogans on Saturday, Hungary's national day, as speakers called for a coalition of the right ahead of next year's elections.
"This government is already finished," playwright turned right-wing politician Istvan Csurka told crowds gathered in the capital's majestic Heroes' square.
Hungary's Socialist-Free Democrat coalition came to power in May 1994 and has a 72 percent majority in parliament.
But recent opinion polls showed parties of the right steadily gaining ground, with the Smallholders' Party in the lead.
Government officials attended celebrations throughout the country but Csurka said the rally called by his party, the Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP) had by far the largest appeal.
"There are more people here than at all other (Budapest) venues put together," he said.
Csurka, whose core group of supporters have staged large rallies over the last three years, has toned down his rethoric and speakers included public figures outside MIEP's base.
Opposition politician Agnes Maczo, deputy speaker of parliament said the ruling coalition unjustly accuses the opposition of radicalism.
"If we are radicals, than Sandor Petofi was also a radical," Maczo said.
The poet Petofi was a leader of Hungary's unsuccessful 1848 anti-Habsburg revolution, the outbreak of which is celebrated on March 15.
Csurka's party, which failed to obtain the five percent of votes required for parliament during the last elections, mainly builds on remnants of anti-communist feelings.
Socialist Prime Minister Gyula Horn, a former communist, was a conscript of a militia which helped Soviet troops crush Hungary's 1956 anti-Soviet uprising.
Csurka also spoke against international financial institutions which he said are responsible for worsening living standards.
"The conditions imposed by the World Bank and the IMF on Hungary are impossible to achieve," he said.
